statement: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = x^2 + x + 3$. The table shows some values of the function $g$. $$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ \hline g(x) & 9 & 15 & 23 & 33 \end{array}$$ Which of the following could define $g$?

choices.misconception: I saw that $g(0)$ equals $f(2)$ and decided the graph had moved $2$ units to the right, so I wrote $f(x - 2)$.
I compared only the first column, where $g(0) - f(0) = 9 - 3 = 6$, and did not check the other columns.
I checked only the first two columns, where $3f(0) = 9$ and $3f(1) = 15$, and did not check $x = 2$.

hints: Find $f(0)$, $f(1)$, $f(2)$, and so on, and look for the table's outputs among them.
$g(0) = f(2)$, $g(1) = f(3)$, $g(2) = f(4)$ and $g(3) = f(5)$: each output of $g$ is $f$ evaluated $2$ units further along.

solutions.reliable:
The values of $f$ are $f(2) = 9$, $f(3) = 15$, $f(4) = 23$ and $f(5) = 33$, so $g(x) = f(x + 2)$ for every $x$ in the table. Checking the others: $f(x - 2)$ gives $f(-2) = 5 
e 9$ at $x = 0$; $f(x) + 6$ gives $5 + 6 = 11 
e 15$ at $x = 1$; and $3f(x)$ gives $3 \cdot 9 = 27 
e 23$ at $x = 2$.
